body:
`regrid!` tried the single-dimension paths before the multi-dimensional one. `we_can_regrid_in_x`, `_in_y` and `_in_z` only compare the field sizes in the other two dimensions, so a dimension with the same number of cells but different faces was copied index by index instead of regridded. For example:

- A stretched 4×4×4 `RectilinearGrid` regridded onto a uniform 4×4×2 grid was regridded in `z` only. The stretched `x` and `y` were copied as if they matched the target.
- A `Field{Center, Center, Nothing}` on a `LatitudeLongitudeGrid` that is `Flat` in `z`:
  - With equal horizontal sizes it went to `regrid_in_z!` and threw.
  - With one horizontal size equal, it was regridded only in the other direction, even when both longitude and latitude differed.

This PR:

- **Checks `we_can_regrid_multiple_dimensions` first.** It compares faces per dimension, so every dimension that differs is regridded whatever its size. The single-dimension paths remain as the fallback for cases it rejects, for example grids with different topologies, as in the reduced-field test from #6142.
- **Copies the field with `set!` when no dimension differs.**
- **Compares faces exactly in `dimension_differs`.** The default `isapprox` tolerance (about 3.5e-4 relative in `Float32`) treats a subcell longitude shift as no change, which would now copy instead of regrid.

New tests:

- A stretched `RectilinearGrid` source regridded onto uniform targets whose sizes match in some dimensions and not others. Each is checked against `brute_force_regrid` and for conservation of the integral.
- `LatitudeLongitudeGrid` 2D fields with shifted longitude and latitude ranges.
- An identical grid with a different halo, which must copy the values exactly.
- Subcell longitude shifts in each float type.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Regrid every dimension whose coordinates differ

body:
This PR reduces the cost of the ZWENO overflow protection introduced in #6015, uses fused multiply-adds in the reconstruction, and normalizes the weights with backend-selected division in Float32/BFloat16 (ordinary division in Float64).

For Float32/BFloat16, replace the minimum-smoothness-based rescaling with `ϵ★ = max(ϵ, τ * 2⁻⁶²)`:

```
αᵣ = C★ᵣ * (1 + (τ / (βᵣ + ϵ★))²)
ωᵣ = αᵣ * newton_div(WCT, one(Σα), Σα)    # Float32/BFloat16; Float64 uses αᵣ * (1 / Σα)
```

The guard bounds the ratio by approximately 2⁶² and its squared weighted sum by approximately 2¹²⁴, avoiding overflow and keeping the normalization reciprocal normal in Float32/BFloat16. It costs one multiply and one `max` per reconstruction and is inactive unless `τ > 2⁶²ϵ ≈ 4.6e10`. Float64 retains the constant regularization.

Fused multiply-adds are used in `biased_p`, the higher-order global smoothness indicators, and `1 + r²`. In Float32 and BFloat16, both normalization paths use the configured weight-computation division: `NormalDivision` retains ordinary division, while `BackendOptimizedDivision` uses an approximate reciprocal on CUDA. Float64 always normalizes with ordinary division, because the approximate reciprocal pushes the Float64 tracer tendency kernel past an occupancy threshold (see below). The reconstruction adds weighted first-difference corrections to an unweighted anchor, preserving constants even when the weights do not sum exactly to one; this does not by itself establish stability or high-order accuracy.

### Controlled normalization benchmark

An A100-SXM4-80GB comparison isolates normalization between `c323bf5e8` (approximate) and `a6086572a` (ordinary). Both retain identical overflow protection, fused multiply-adds, and `BackendOptimizedDivision` for the α ratios. Each uses the same GPU and locked dependencies, warmed compilation, synchronized timing, and four alternating A/B passes. Grid size is 256×256×128. Times are medians in milliseconds per tendency evaluation; the ratio is ordinary / approximate.

| Float32 workload | Approximate | Ordinary | Ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Scalar WENO5 | 0.434433 | 0.512682 | 1.18012 |
| Scalar WENO7 | 0.710061 | 0.750877 | 1.05748 |
| Scalar WENO9 | 1.115618 | 1.175360 | 1.05355 |
| Breeze full-model WENO7 | 4.703989 | 5.096128 | 1.08336 |

Across these workloads, the coefficient of variation of the four pass ratios was 0.007–0.021%. The Breeze workload uses the existing rest-state benchmark setup. BFloat16 ordinary / approximate ratios were 1.62, 1.24, and 1.20 for WENO5/7/9. Float64 differences were below 0.8% and changed sign with order.

Reactant was measured separately with `raise=true` and explicit `BackendOptimizedDivision`: WENO7 was effectively unchanged; WENO9 favored ordinary normalization by 0.66%; WENO5 was noisy and inconclusive. These results do not establish a Reactant speedup. Earlier whole-PR measurements also showed slower Breeze Reactant tendencies at WENO7/9 versus main, so that performance caveat remains.

Benchmark software: Julia 1.13.0, CUDA.jl 6.2.2, KernelAbstractions.jl 0.9.44, Breeze 0.11.3. Both variants shared a CUDA runtime/system-library version warning (configured runtime 12.9, system toolkit/driver API 12.4). The benchmark predates the latest main merge; it measures the isolated normalization change rather than the entire current PR versus main.

The report, raw data, scripts, manifests, and Slurm logs are retained on `gcp-slurm` at `~/pr6209-normalization-benchmark.md` and `~/pr6209-normalization-benchmark/`.

### Float64: ordinary normalization

With approximate normalization in every precision (`6824b4a00`), the CI benchmark slowed the Float64 tracer tendency kernels by about 31% (`gpu_compute_hydrostatic_free_surface_Gc_`, 0.944 → 1.24 ms; the main baseline reproduced to 0.1% across runs), while Gu/Gv sped up by 7–10% and Float32 throughput improved from +1.9% to +7.6% versus main.

An A100 kernel-level comparison of the EarthOcean tripolar 360×180×50 WENO7 CATKE 2-tracer configuration attributes this to register pressure. Approximate normalization raises the Float64 Gc kernel from 128 to 147 registers per thread. With 256-thread blocks, 128 registers is the most that fits two blocks per SM, so occupancy halves. Gu/Gv already fit only one block (226–244 registers), so they keep the instruction savings. No variant spills. Mean kernel times in ms, averaged over two replicates (which agree within 1% in Float64 and 3–5% in Float32; the Float32 code of the last two rows is identical):

| Normalization | F64 Gc | F64 Gu / Gv | F32 Gc | F32 Gu / Gv |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ordinary everywhere | 0.633 (128 regs) | 1.54 / 1.50 | 0.416 | 1.05 / 1.01 |
| approximate everywhere (`6824b4a00`) | 0.885 (147 regs) | 1.45 / 1.33 | 0.371 | 0.97 / 0.86 |
| **this PR: ordinary in F64, approximate in F32** | **0.630 (128 regs)** | 1.53 / 1.49 | 0.375 | 0.98 / 0.87 |
| folding 1/Σα into the reconstruction | 0.874 (150 regs) | 1.44 / 1.32 | 0.376 | 1.04 / 0.91 |

Folding the division into the reconstruction does not reduce register pressure, so it was not adopted. The Float64 dispatch gives up the Gu/Gv gain; recovering it without the Gc penalty requires changing occupancy (block size or a register cap), which affects every kernel and belongs in a separate PR. Register counts are configuration-specific, so other closures may sit on either side of the threshold.

Correctness on the A100: the Float64 dispatch is bitwise identical to ordinary normalization in tendencies and state; in Float32 it is bitwise identical to approximate normalization, and differs from ordinary normalization by at most 8e-13 in absolute tendency. No variant produced non-finite values. Report and data: `~/pr6209-f64-registers/` on `gcp-slurm`.

### Validation

- CPU `unit/weno_smoothness` and `unit/weno_smoothness_reference`: 4,608 checks pass after restoring approximate normalization on the latest PR branch.
- CPU `unit/weno_smoothness` and `unit/weno_smoothness_reference`: 4,608 checks pass with the Float64 ordinary-normalization dispatch (`03da76e1c`).
- CPU `unit/quality_assurance`: all 107 Aqua, ExplicitImports, and Core.Box checks pass.
- A100 numerical comparisons at the benchmark commits: all tested tendencies finite; maximum relative differences of 1.49e-7 (Float32), 6.94e-17 (Float64), and 3.83e-5 (BFloat16). The retained Breeze rest-state tendencies were bitwise identical.
- A100 overflow-guard cases with jumps of 3e5, 1e7, and 1e15: all 1,152 output values per variant finite and bitwise identical across variants.
- Earlier GPU suites passed on `c323bf5e8`: weno_smoothness, weno_smoothness_reference, bounds_preserving_advection, adaptive_implicit_vertical_advection, immersed_advection, regression/nonhydrostatic, regression/hydrostatic, enzyme, and reactant/correctness. These broader suites have not been rerun locally on the latest main merge.
